draft.title: Status
card: Status
Status is the social position a person holds in a group or society. It often brings a level of respect or standing.
Ascribed status
a position a person is given, usually at birth or without choosing it. Examples are age, sex and family background.
Achieved status
a position a person earns through effort, choices or skills. Examples are a job, a qualification or a sporting title.
One person holds many statuses at once. A 16-year-old (ascribed) who is school captain (achieved) holds both kinds.
draft.remember: Ascribed status comes without choosing it. Achieved status is earned.

a.q: Which of these is an example of an achieved status?
opts: Becoming a qualified electrician
Being the eldest child in a family
Being born into a well-known family
Being a teenager in Australia
a.why: Becoming an electrician is earned through study and training. Being the eldest child is a position given by birth, so it is ascribed, even though it can seem like a role a person grows into.
a.clue: Which one did the person work towards?

b.q: Priya was born into a family of farmers in Wagga Wagga. She studied hard and became a veterinarian. Which statement is correct?
opts: Family background is ascribed and being a vet is achieved
Family background is achieved and being a vet is ascribed
Both family background and being a vet are ascribed
Both family background and being a vet are achieved
b.why: Priya did not choose the family she was born into, so that status is ascribed. She earned her vet qualification through study, so that status is achieved. Her family background is not achieved just because it shaped her path.
b.clue: Ask which status she chose and which she was given.

b.best: Family background is ascribed and being a vet is achieved

problems.detail: The right option is the only one that starts with 'Becoming' rather than 'Being', and the only one with the detail 'qualified'. That wording signals something earned, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.
